1jehuang/jcode ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v0.94.0 Stable2026-10-10T13:19:02Z

Queued commands

Highlights

  • Ctrl+Enter queues slash and ! commands to run after the current turn, and /clear drops anything still queued
  • Alt+G opens the project's git commit log, and diff cycling moves to /diff
  • Harness API clients can observe and cancel messages sent mid-turn

Improvements

  • The startup frame settles immediately instead of popping in over about 200ms, with session facts shown on the first frame
  • The Overview widget stays visible after startup
  • Onboarding is cleaner: side-by-side start choice, no starter prompt cards, and the home directory is labeled '~ (home)'
  • Onboarding detects accounts you are signed in with in Cursor, other AI tools, and stored Jcode agent logins
  • Restored transcripts and the session picker preview no longer show a redundant 'tool:' summary line

Fixes

  • Escaped single-word brackets like [workspace] are no longer rendered as display math
  • Onboarding's Import option no longer commits when pressing Enter, and toggling preview no longer flickers the screen
  • Sleep inhibition keeps its lock across refreshes and retries after helper failures

Full changelog: https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/compare/v0.93.0...v0.94.0

phuryn/pm-skills ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v2.2.0 Stable2026-10-10T10:56:34Z

v2.2.0 — 2026-10-10

pm-execution

  • create-prd is now lean by default: a first PRD is about one to two pages, with the detailed version on request. Feedback was that the skill fought itself, asking for a "comprehensive" document and for brevity at the same time. "Complete" now means no gap that blocks a decision about the first version; the section questions are a checklist to pick from rather than a form to fill; Market Segments and Value Propositions are always included; unknowns go to Assumptions and open questions instead of being invented; it asks up to three questions when the problem, the users, or the success metric is missing; it researches the market, competitors, and alternatives freely, citing sources, and puts a finding in the PRD only when it changes a decision; and it ends by naming what it left out so you can expand any section. The Value Proposition section now uses the 6-part JTBD template (Who, Why, What before, How, What after, Alternatives, by Paweł Huryn and Aatir Abdul Rauf), one per segment (two or three segments at most for a first version), and is the spine of the PRD: the Solution delivers its How and the Key Results measure its What after. It also gained a short checklist for reviewing an existing PRD.
  • /write-prd now uses the create-prd template. It had carried its own, different 8-section template while also invoking the skill. It asks at most three questions up front.

pm-ai-shipping

  • Added the code-review skill: correctness is the core engine, with performance and security as optional sub-cases of it rather than separate methods. It anchors on agreements between participants across a boundary — the defects that stay invisible file-by-file because each side reads as reasonable alone — forces a violating execution, and refutes every candidate before reporting.
  • Added a correctness taxonomy reference built from real fix history, plus performance and security reference sheets the same engine reads.
  • /ship-check gained a correctness review as Step 3, before the security and performance audits, and an independent unsteered pass by a second model as Step 6.
  • /security-audit-static gained an OWASP Top 10 coverage backstop: every surviving finding is mapped to a category, and any category with zero findings is flagged "not covered — double-check" rather than silently passing. It is a coverage check, not a mandate to invent findings.
  • Docs, the test-coverage map and reports now follow the host repo's setup. Before writing, the kit reads the repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and what they import), its docs folder, and any existing equivalent of each document under any name; it updates those instead of creating parallel files and keeps their naming and date conventions. documentation/, documentation/tests.md, reports/ and the default file names apply only where the repo has none, and the output says so. It never creates a file that differs from an existing one only in letter case (tests.md beside TESTS.md), which collides on Windows and macOS. The rule lives once, in the shipping-artifacts skill.
  • /ship-check edits the agent instruction file the repo already uses. Where one of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md only imports or points to the other (a CLAUDE.md that is just @AGENTS.md), it edits the file pointed to and leaves the pointer alone; where only one exists, it edits that one. CLAUDE.md plus a thin AGENTS.md is created only in a repo with neither.
  • The independent review in /ship-check Step 6 is a fresh session of a model family different from the one that built the code, using the reviewer the repo's own instructions name. It no longer names a specific model as the usual choice.
  • /derive-tests defers to the repo's stated gate policy. A repo whose instructions make the gate a local command plus a human go keeps that: the coverage map records the policy and whether the deterministic tests run inside it, instead of recommending hosted CI and branch protection over it. The green-before-merge CI gate remains the recommendation where the repo states no policy.
  • /derive-tests writes into an existing file only when that file is a test-coverage map. A TESTS.md that describes the repo's testing method is no longer taken for the map just because of its name: the kit matches on what a file covers, uses the repo's real coverage map, and where there is none picks a name that collides with nothing, rather than writing into a same-named file about something else.
  • /document-app check is a check-only mode for a repo that keeps its docs by hand as intent. It writes no file and reports each place where an existing doc and the code disagree: the doc says X, the code does Y, with file:line on both sides. It doesn't decide which side is wrong; the owner decides whether to fix the code or the doc. The output ends with a short summary a release checklist can cite.
  • /derive-tests check does the same for the coverage map. It writes no file, reads the tests without running them, and reports rows that are stale against the docs or the test suite (a documented rule with no row, an "existing" row whose test is gone, a test the map doesn't credit), ending with the same kind of citable summary.
  • /security-audit-static and /performance-audit-static can audit only a change: pass a git range (/security-audit-static v2.1.0..HEAD), changes for the uncommitted working tree, or both. The audit covers the changed files plus what the change makes newly reachable or newly wrong elsewhere, not the whole codebase. A release normally audits only its changes; a whole-repository audit, still the default with no argument, is for the first release or after a large refactor.

farion1231/cc-switch ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v4.0.7CC Switch v4.0.7 Stable2026-10-10T09:11:51Z

CC Switch v4.0.7

4.0 正式版的第三个修复版本

同一个 OpenAI 账号下的 Plus 和 Team 工作区，在 4.0 里切不过去，这个版本修好了。额度可以改回 3.x 那样显示「已用」，在「设置 → 通用 → 外观」里切换。Codex 的历史会话可以在 CC Switch 里打开压缩，会话管理和用量统计也能读取压缩后的会话。直连和路由互相切换后，CC Switch 也会提示重启 Codex；Windows 上第一次能看到这条提示。用量统计这次修了几处算错的地方，包括 Claude 1 小时缓存写入的价格和部分中转站的缓存命中。4.0 完整的更新内容请见 v4.0 发布说明。

English → | 日本語版 →

新增

可以压缩 Codex 的历史会话。 Codex 会把每个会话完整记录在 ~/.codex/sessions 下，用得多的话这个目录会涨到几十 GB。Codex 自己有一个还在开发中的压缩功能，默认关闭；CC Switch 这次加了开关，并且能读取压缩后的会话。

  • 怎么打开： 在「设置 → 应用配置 → Codex」打开「压缩 Codex 历史会话」，旁边会显示 sessions 和 archived_sessions 两个目录当前一共占多少空间。这个开关直接改 Codex 的 config.toml：打开时写入 [features] 下的 local_thread_store_compression = true，关闭时删掉这一行，CC Switch 不另外保存这个设置。
  • 压缩什么时候发生： 打开后不会马上压缩。Codex 每次启动时会在后台把 7 天以上没动过的会话文件压成同名的 .jsonl.zst，再删掉原文件。实测压缩后大约只占原来的六分之一。
  • 继续旧会话： 照常在 Codex 里继续就行，Codex 会先把这个会话解压回原来的格式。
  • 在 CC Switch 里： 压缩过的会话照常出现在会话列表里，可以查看和删除，用量照常统计，压缩前后也不会重复计算。为了在会话很多时也能很快打开列表，CC Switch 只读压缩文件的开头，所以这些会话不显示最后一条回复的预览，最后活跃时间取文件的修改时间。
  • 需要注意： 需要较新版本的 Codex，改完要重启 Codex 才生效。这是 Codex 还在开发中的功能，打开后 Codex 每次启动都会显示一条提示。关闭开关后不再压缩新的会话，已经压缩的会话保持原样，只有在 Codex 里继续时才会被解压。其他直接读取 .jsonl 会话文件的工具可能读不到压缩后的会话。

即使不打开这个开关，Codex 的后台服务也可能自己压缩会话。以前 CC Switch 只认未压缩的会话文件，这些会话会从会话列表里消失，用量也不会导入，现在都能正常读取。

额度可以显示「已用」。 4.0 把各档额度都改成了「剩余 x%」，有人习惯 3.x 的「已用 x%」，也有人希望和 Codex 自己的写法一致，所以做成了设置。在「设置 → 通用 → 外观 → 额度显示」选「剩余」（默认）或「已用」，供应商卡片、授权中心和托盘都会跟着变。只有各档的百分比会换，余额、Codex Credits 和重置次数始终显示剩余，用完的档位仍然显示「已用完」。颜色和「快用完」提醒仍然按剩余算，已用 94% 和剩余 6% 一样是橙色。展开后的进度条长度跟着显示的数字走，已用 30% 就画 30%。

直连和路由互相切换后，也会提示重启 Codex。 已经打开的 Codex 还在用启动时读到的模型列表。以前只在聚合模式下检查，直连和路由互相切换后，即使模型列表变了也不会提示。现在三种模式都会检查。关掉提示后如果模型列表又变了，提示会再次出现。

Windows 上也能看到重启 Codex 的提示了。 以前判断 Codex 有没有在运行，靠读系统进程列表，这个方法在 Windows 上用不了，模型列表和账号的提示都不会出现，重启按钮也总是说后台服务没在运行。现在 Windows 上按 Codex 后台服务自己记录的进程号判断它是否在运行，只在确认它在运行时提供重启按钮。CC Switch 在 Windows 上看不到 Codex 桌面版和编辑器插件，所以只要模型列表或登录账号和你上次关掉提示时不一样，就会提示「切换前就开着的 Codex 可能还在用之前的账号或模型列表」；这些客户端没开着的话，直接关掉提示就行。刚升级时不会弹出这条提示。

从应用页菜单打开「配置目录」时，设置页会滚到这个应用的条目，并让它的边框闪两下。滚动途中你自己滚动或点击，会马上停止；系统开启了减少动态效果时直接跳过去。

修复

  • 同一个 OpenAI 账号下的 Plus 和 Team 工作区，在 Codex 里切不过去。 4.0 只按用户来认 Codex 的官方登录，同一个人的不同工作区被当成「已经登录了这个账号」，auth.json 不会改写，也不会提示重启。暂存登录信息时也按用户记，同一个人的几个工作区只剩一份。现在按「用户 + 工作区」来认，和 Codex 自己判断账号有没有变的方式一致。升级后会自动整理暂存的登录信息，被合并掉的工作区会从官方卡片里找回来；已经登出的账号不会被恢复。
  • Codex 供应商的地址写在 config.toml 顶层时，编辑保存会把地址删掉。 这类配置在编辑器里请求地址显示为空，保存后地址被删除，路由报「Codex Provider 缺少 base_url 配置」；直连模式下切过去还会走到 OpenAI 官方地址。现在会把顶层地址整理到 [model_providers.custom] 里，编辑器能显示，保存也会保留。表单也不再生成这种写法。
  • Windows 用户名里有中文等非 ASCII 字符时，在「应用」页升级工具失败，提示「系统找不到指定的路径」。Claude Code 供应商卡片上的「打开终端」也会读不到临时配置，Claude Code 不报错，直接用默认配置启动；项目目录带中文时也一样。原因是 CC Switch 生成的批处理文件按 UTF-8 写入，cmd.exe 却按控制台代码页读。升级脚本现在会先切换到 UTF-8，这一步只在它自己的隐藏窗口里生效；「打开终端」不切换代码页（那会改掉你自己终端的设置），改为不把这些路径直接写进批处理文件。
  • Codex 在官方供应商下继续旧的第三方会话时，报错提示让你重启。 Codex 继续会话时会沿用会话创建时的供应商，第三方会话会一直指向本地路由，重启 Codex 也没用。现在报错会说明这是旧的第三方会话，需要新开会话；只有确实是 Codex 没有重新读取配置时，才提示重启。
  • Claude 的 1 小时缓存写入按 5 分钟的价格计费。 1 小时缓存写入的单价是输入价的 2 倍，5 分钟的是 1.25 倍，以前一律按 5 分钟算，少算了不少。现在代理日志和 Claude Code 会话导入都会分开计价。
  • 部分 OpenAI 兼容中转站的缓存命中显示为 0。 有的中转站把 cache_read_input_tokens 固定写成 0，真实命中数放在 prompt_cache_hit_tokens 里，以前读到 0 就不往下找了，缓存命中显示为 0，未命中的输入也被多算。现在遇到 0 会接着看下一个字段。Claude Code 经路由转 OpenAI Chat 格式、Codex 和 Grok Build 使用 Chat 格式的上游时都按这个规则读。
  • Codex 会话导入的用量里没有缓存写入。 GPT-5.6 和 GPT-6 的缓存写入被按普通输入计价，现在会单独记录。
  • Claude Sonnet 5.5 和 Haiku 5.5 的费用记为 0。 内置定价表补上了这两个模型。
  • 用量统计「Claude」页里，同一个供应商在 Claude Code 和 Claude Desktop 里都配置过时，会出现两行一样的记录，切换应用后还会留下旧的行。
  • OpenCode 和 MiniMax Code 的额外选项，编辑其中一项后，其他没动过的值类型会变。 比如字符串 "123"、"false" 被存成数字或布尔值。现在没改过的值保持原样，改名时也不能改成已有的名字。
  • OpenClaw 打开或关闭「发送 User-Agent」时，其他自定义请求头全被删掉。 现在只改 User-Agent 这一项。
  • Pi 和 MiniMax Code 的「火山 Agent Plan」预设用的是 Coding Plan 的地址，Agent Plan 的 Key 用不了。现在改用 Agent Plan 自己的地址，另外新增「火山 Coding Plan」预设。

其他：

  • 中文版聚合模式指南和三语用户手册补充了两个 Codex 常见问题：子 agent 换到另一家供应商后读不到任务，以及官方 5 小时额度用完后 /model 被锁定在 Luna Reserve，暂时把第三方供应商设为默认可以绕开。
  • 「统一 Codex 会话历史」的说明改为只针对 Codex CLI：Codex 桌面版更新后已经能显示所有供应商的会话，只用桌面版的话不需要打开。

升级说明

数据库结构没有变化，仍然是 20。

Claude 的缓存写入费用升级后会变高。 用 1 小时缓存时（Claude Code 主会话通常就是），新记录的缓存写入按正确的价格计算，每天的费用会比升级前高一截。这是以前少算了，不是涨价；升级前的记录不会重算。

Claude Sonnet 5.5 和 Haiku 5.5 以前记为 0 的费用，会在启动时按新价格补算。Haiku 5.5 只按 10 万 token 以内的价格计算，更长的提示词会少算。

已经添加过的「火山 Agent Plan」供应商（Pi、MiniMax Code）不会自动修改，请把请求地址里的 /api/coding/v3 改成 /api/plan/v3，或者删掉后用新预设重新添加。

致谢

感谢 @ggbdpq（中转站缓存命中显示为 0、OpenCode 额外选项类型被改、直连和路由切换后的重启提示）、@Chaoqi31（报告并修复 Claude 1 小时缓存写入计价、Codex 会话导入缓存写入）、@Yanxcyan（Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 定价、火山 Agent Plan 预设）、@hulkbig（报告并修复 OpenClaw 自定义请求头被删）、@Railgun-wiki（报告并修复用量统计重复行）、@funkpopo（设置页滚到应用配置条目）的贡献。

感谢 @yleo888、@harvey500、@friendlzw、@burningimlam、@JinLin-Yu、@winter-maple、@SamPheng、@cjmarklll、@LeenixP、@EMnian 报告问题和提出建议。

完整的技术细节请见 CHANGELOG。

v1.3.2-rc.2 Prerelease2026-10-10T09:00:43Z

beads v1.3.2-rc.2

Pre-compiled binaries for Linux, macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon), Windows (AMD64 & ARM64), Android/Termux (ARM64), and FreeBSD.

Installation (release candidate)

This is a prerelease for validation. The stable install channels — Homebrew, the install.sh / install.ps1 scripts, npm, and PyPI — intentionally keep serving the latest stable release, so they will not install this RC. Use one of the methods below.

Manual download (recommended): Download the archive for your platform from the Assets below, extract it, and place bd on your PATH.

Go install (pinned to this RC):

go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@v1.3.2-rc.2
# For embedded Dolt support:
CGO_ENABLED=1 GOFLAGS=-tags=gms_pure_go go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@v1.3.2-rc.2

When you are done validating, return to the stable release through your normal channel (e.g. brew upgrade beads).

heygen-com/hyperframes ↗ 2 releases · 2 stable
v0.8.145 Stable2026-10-10T08:28:04Z

HyperFrames v0.8.145

Released on 2026-10-10.

Studio can export on the GPU, and the producer package on npm is a fraction of its old size. Long exports no longer stall at 90%, and previews recover from a stalled font or asset.

Features

  • Studio: Export can encode on the GPU, like render --gpu (91f9c9eb0, #5397).

Fixes

  • Producer: The npm package ships only its own code and no source maps (affa4d53c, #5398).
  • Examples: The k8s chunk-runner image installs and loads the producer again (6f3f86a9c, #5373).
  • Studio Server: The public proxy cache path names boxed preview copies too (e158c73a9, #5407).
  • CLI: Keyframes --shot on a compositions/ file mounts the scene in its project (4225fba3a, #5401).
  • Skills: Skill scripts run through a symlinked skills dir and agents keep long renders alive (f46033d04, #5396).
  • Runtime: Graded pictures stay graded in sandboxed players (684c03848, #5383).
  • Engine: Audio duration probe reads to the end on Windows; cli tests skip bun's disk cache (3d6de0581, #5395).
  • Engine: Long exports with many clips no longer stall at 90% or hide a timeout (4b68f73fe, #5375).
  • Studio: A stalled font or asset no longer leaves the preview empty or drops reloads (d93b76976, #5370).
  • Studio Server: A failed save reports its real error when a later file was never written (063c2f8d6, #5364).

Full changelog

https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/compare/v0.8.144...v0.8.145

View release →

v0.8.144 Stable2026-10-10T01:10:24Z

HyperFrames v0.8.144

Released on 2026-10-10.

Previews are steadier and the CLI is more reliable on Windows. Small previews keep every layer, a looping scene no longer plays past the film's end, and transcribe can write SRT or VTT directly.

Features

  • CLI: Let transcribe --to write srt or vtt straight from a media file (908f4395b, #5215).
  • CLI: Models list shows which speech models transcribe can use (0576b24c7, #5323).

Fixes

  • Core: Stop small previews dropping layers on heavy compositions (5562c280d, #5268).
  • Studio: The timeline viewport gate gives the same verdict on the same code (2c082b3fe, #5361).
  • Engine: Recover audio duration by decoding the final frame (9460c983e, #3986).
  • Core: A data script in a sub-composition no longer stops every timeline (e1b60933d, #5205).
  • Lint: Check passes valid sub-compositions and scene-relative asset paths (5ec2dd2e1, #5337).
  • CLI: Mirror skills into every installed agent on Windows (ce73339b1, #5367).
  • CLI: Renders on Windows stop cancelling when an old parent's pid is reused (ce359d91c, #5358).
  • Studio: A resized corner stays on the pointer when the size rounds to whole pixels (6b341b0d8, #5213).
  • CLI: Name the unzip errors when every Windows unzip tool fails (024107856, #5355).
  • Studio Server: The preview's proxy copy jumps queued thumbnails, and abandoned copies drop (5eb2a96fc, #5340).
  • CLI: Preserve subtitle cues across line endings (9c1d3fbe6, #5223).
  • CLI: Undo complete timeline batch receipts atomically (d03e41c9b, #5279).
  • Studio: Clip strips resize on the next frame, ending ResizeObserver loop errors (a1803448b, #5187).
  • Core: Preview stops at the film's end when a scene loops forever (cea48a548, #5320).
  • CLI: Browser ensure fails when the unzip leaves no Chrome executable (577bdf670, #5329).
  • Sdk: Correct animation calls in examples and docs (a03d709a5, #5247).
  • Studio: Let small picks move when dragged by their middle (7a84d29df, #5206).

Performance

  • Engine: Wait for a missing composition timeline once per render, not once per browser (e25394d38, #5227).

Docs & Examples

  • Clarify async font measurement and timeline registration (9e69821b8, #5203).

Catalog

  • Ci: Keep the catalog publish PR when main changes nothing it generates (7b85b2840, #5372).
  • CLI: Reject a swallowed --json when catalog's string flags have no value (1de8b5ae3, #3992).
  • Catalog: Compare search vectors by direction so the publish PR can pass (6ae1af747, #5359).
  • Registry: Seven more WebGPU shader backgrounds, from sun burst to color wheel (b05960008, #5341).
  • Registry: Seven more WebGPU shader backgrounds, from ripples to thin film (9dbbca745, #5190).
  • Registry: Eight more WebGPU shader backgrounds, from blob to fractal noise (46f6cb356, #5192).
  • Registry: Eight more WebGPU shader backgrounds and a bundle with thirty new shaders (63a7ec692, #5191).

Internal

  • Engine: Real-ffmpeg tests and fixture cleanup get a 30 s budget (6a83959b0, #5368).
  • Image builds pull through a mirror instead of rate-limited Docker Hub (70c873a70, #5377).

Full changelog

https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/compare/v0.8.143...v0.8.144

career-ops-v1.36.0career-ops v1.36.0: Through the Filter Stable2026-10-10T06:53:08Z

<!-- co:release-notes:career-ops-v1.36.0 --> This release is about getting through the filter: eight more places to find openings, and a CV that applicant tracking systems read the way you wrote it.

Highlights

  • Eight new job sources. ADP Workforce Now, Dayforce, Taleo and UKG Pro by @Schlaflied (#3729, #3734, #3743, #3733), JazzHR by @ilyakanevskiy (#4307), Gupy by @felipe-NR (#4550), startup.jobs by @phozzy (#4704) and PageUp by @williamchong (#4693). Eightfold boards now return their jobs instead of zero, by @kellymmcgrath (#4297).
  • A CV the ATS reads correctly. pdf --ats writes a plain ATS variant next to the styled CV, by @vliggio (#4909). atsLint checks a template against ATS rules kept as data in templates/ats-rules.yml, by @rubicon (#3900). A CV structure check by @euskode (#3472), a title-consistency check by @Schlaflied (#2678), and a flag for inflated scope verbs and unsourced adoption claims by @MannXo (#3784). Hyphenated terms like "go-to-market" no longer split across lines in the PDF, by @Kevin-Boyle (#4911).
  • More markets. A Singapore market mode by @jpelaez-23blocks (#4687), and language.modes_dir can now list several markets at once, by @Schlaflied (#3798).
  • The web dashboard. Local scheduled scans by @aselekoglu (#2628), Analytics progress and insights read from the core by @abankar1 (#4576), and assistant conversations that keep their earlier context by @luochen211 (#4495).
  • Optional GDPR consent footer for CVs ({{CONSENT}}), by @drawski (#4286).

Your agent offers this update at the start of your next session. If it doesn't, run this once in your career-ops folder:

node update-system.mjs apply --confirm

Your CV, profile, tracker and reports are not touched.

Thank you

This release carries 211 pull requests from 68 people, 20 of them contributing for the first time.

cua-driver-rs-v0.34.1cua-driver-rs: v0.34.1 Prerelease2026-10-09T17:20:37Z

Cua Driver 0.34.1

Summary

This release adds 2 features and includes 2 fixes.

Features

  • capture GNOME windows from their own actor (WinRects v10). (#4895)
  • add display_only to get_window_state for live previews. (#4895)

Fixes

  • pass CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND through to embedded hosts. (#4895)
  • wait for EIS to acknowledge libei input before replying. (#4895)

Performance

  • reuse one session-bus connection for the GNOME helper. (#4895) Thanks @injaneity, @louistiti.

Contributors

Thanks to @injaneity, @louistiti for contributing to this release.

Install

macOS and Linux:

/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"

Windows:

irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds, and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and uninstaller scripts.

Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest” pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned cua-driver-rs-v* releases directly.

stablyai/orca ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v1.4.224 Stable2026-10-10T04:30:28Z

Thank you so much for using Orca and for your continued support! ❤️

The short version

  • Automations can now set the agent's model and effort for each run. In the automation editor, open Advanced and fill in Extra agent arguments (or use --extra-agent-args with orca automations create and edit), for example -model haiku --effort high. This works today for Claude, Codex, Grok and CodeBuddy (model and effort), Cursor (model, which carries its effort) and OMP (model), and support for more agents is coming soon. Each run starts a fresh session, and your other automations keep the host's defaults. Separately, scheduled runs in an existing workspace on an Orca server now hand the task to agents that read it after they start, such as Aider, Goose and Amp, instead of leaving them idle.
  • SSH hosts now run a managed Orca server. Orca ships its own runtime and sets it up when you connect, so connections no longer fail because a host has the wrong Node version or no build tools. A host with no open terminals switches on its next connect and brings its projects, folders and open editor tabs along. A host with open terminals keeps working as before and offers Move to a managed Orca server, which restarts those terminals. A host that can't run it keeps its current connection, and Settings → SSH Hosts says why. You can see, update, roll back, Recover or Forget each server in Settings → Managed servers.
  • Native chat (experimental): If you turned on Chat UI with chat as your default view, supported agents now open in the structured chat by default. If Terminal was your default, new agent tabs stay in the terminal, and a one-time tip explains the change and lets you turn chat mode on. You can move a conversation between chat and a terminal from the tab's right-click menu or from Agent Session History (Resume in New CLI / Resume in New Native Chat).
  • More in native chat: Recent versions of OpenCode (including 2.x), Pi and OMP open as structured chats on this computer. Agents can draw charts, diagrams and mockups right inside a reply, on desktop and phone (switch it off under Settings → Chat → Inline visuals). Cmd/Ctrl+F searches a chat, you can quote part of a reply with Add to chat, Up/Down recalls every prompt you sent, number keys answer an agent's questions, and long messages and runs of tool calls fold into one row. The model picker no longer waits for the agent to start, Codex and Pi say they're signed out before you send, and a reply Orca had to cut off says why and offers Continue. Grok shows its subagents, and Grok, OpenCode and OMP can /compact.
  • SSH and remote terminals: Keys you type during a network outage arrive exactly once and in order, scrollback and pane size survive a reconnect, and open tabs reattach after a managed server update. Shell startup files that print text, folders with tens of thousands of entries and 64-bit ARM Linux servers no longer break or drop the connection. Files, browser tabs, links and drag-and-drop stay on the machine they belong to when two machines share a path. orca serve now loads its SSH hosts, and quitting a window on a serving machine no longer stops the server.
  • Phone: A browser tab opened on the phone loads while the desktop is minimized or in its screen saver, chat visuals and subagents show in the phone's native chat, and videos and music files play in previews.
  • Workspaces and editing: You can attach several pull requests, merge requests and tasks to one workspace. Hovering a tab shows its full title with icon and program, Force Delete can remember Always force delete, and Continue in New Session is now Hand Off to Another Agent. Markdown shows GitHub-style callouts such as > [!NOTE], PDFs zoom with pinch and Cmd/Ctrl+=/-, and files dragged in from Finder or File Explorer land in the exact pane, folder or editor you drop them on.
  • Also: The usage meters in the status bar now default to a shorter Compact view unless you chose one (Detailed is still available), Stage All stages every change even when the list is capped at 1,000, and Orca detects the GitHub CLI even when a gh launcher hangs.

Known issues

The orca command on SSH hosts: By default, orca commands run on an SSH host reach only that host's own terminals and orchestration messages. To let agents there create worktrees, open terminals or dispatch work through orca, turn on Allow this host's orca CLI to control Orca for that host (Settings → SSH Hosts → edit the host → Advanced Connection) (#26483).

Downgrading to v1.4.223: Terminals started in v1.4.224 can't be reached from v1.4.223 until you update again. Extra pull requests, merge requests and tasks you attached to a folder workspace are removed. If Chat UI was on, it may be off after you update again; turn it back on in Settings → Experimental. SSH hosts that moved to a managed server work over the old connection in v1.4.223; if you add or remove projects there, the host shows "Changed on an older Orca" after you update and offers Move the new projects. Orca still refuses to install versions older than v1.4.214 from its version picker. To go back to one of those, run orca profile state rollback --latest-json with Orca closed, then install the old version by hand (#23262).

Terminals after updating: This version starts a new terminal background service for new terminals. Terminals that were already open keep running on the previous one, so changes in this release apply only to terminals opened after the update.

Native chats from v1.4.217 or older: If you used native chat (experimental) on v1.4.217 or older and update straight to v1.4.224, your earlier native chats won't appear. Their files stay on disk (#26038).

Relaunching from shell history: When an agent's launch command is long or spans several lines, the shell history holds a short one-time line instead, so pressing up-arrow and Enter does not start the agent again (#23962).

Workspaces created from the phone: Creating a workspace from an issue, pull request or Linear item with an agent on the phone still moves the desktop to that workspace (#26025).

Windows on ARM: The ARM64 package ships an x64 orca.exe command-line tool. Windows 11 on ARM runs it under emulation. Windows 10 on ARM can't run it, so the orca command does not work there (#24094).

OpenCode 2: If you update from v1.4.219 or earlier, OpenCode 2 panes that were already running may show no status until you restart OpenCode in them. If you downgrade Orca after updating, duplicate OpenCode status plugins are left behind. After opencode run exits, its pane can keep showing "Done"; a fix is pending in #24472.

Claude folder trust: Folder pre-trust is on by default (Settings → Agents → "Trust the folder when Orca starts an agent"). On Alpine WSL, Orca can't copy the file permissions it needs, so Claude shows its own trust prompt instead (#23744).

Automations

Each automation can set its own model and effort, and server-run automations in an existing workspace now deliver their task to agents that read it after they start.

Performance & reliability

Less CPU and memory for terminal redraws, checkpoints, Codex output and chat recovery, and profile saves that warn instead of failing on a slow disk.

Graphify-Labs/graphify ↗ 2 releases · 2 stable
v0.9.84 Stable2026-10-10T00:53:14Z

A correctness batch picked directly from open issues, plus an OpenCode plugin fix.

  • Fix: PowerShell functions (and classes/enums) defined inside a file-scope begin {} / process {} / end {} block are now extracted. These blocks parse as pseudo-commands rather than named blocks, so the walker returned before descending and dropped everything inside — the common [CmdletBinding()] advanced-function layout (#4270).
  • Fix: R every backtick-quoted binding now gets a collision-free id. A partially-symbolic name like `%foo%` (or an S3 method `[.cls`, or a dotted `my.op`) normalized to the same id as an ordinary identifier and was silently dropped on merge; such names now use the reserved operator namespace (#4253). (The separate infinite-loop reported in that issue was already fixed in 0.9.83.)
  • Fix: graphify path and the MCP shortest_path tool now fail closed on a file::symbol endpoint whose file defines no such symbol, instead of falling back to scoring the bare name and answering from a same-named symbol in another file; the refusal lists the files that do define it (#4264).
  • Fix: OpenCode the plugin now loads on OpenCode 2 (a default export with setup()) while keeping the v1 server() hook, and graphify install refreshes an already-installed v1-only copy, so the graph tools appear again for users upgraded past the v1 plugin contract (#3554, #3732, thanks @bercedev).
  • Fix: Python a bare import logging is no longer captured by a loose same-named module (scripts/logging.py) in a non-package directory — it resolves to the stdlib module. Guarded by a vendored, deterministic stdlib-name set across the module resolver, the sibling-repoint pass, and the build-time stem-alias index; a deliberate package shadow (logging/__init__.py) still resolves (#4261).
  • Fix: Python a qualified external annotation (httpx.Response) no longer binds to an unrelated private local class (_Response). The stub-rewire match key now preserves underscores, so _Response and Response are distinct identifiers (#4269).
  • Fix: C# an external type the corpus references but never declares (List<T>, System.Type, Unity's VisualElement) now gets one shared, name-keyed placeholder instead of a separate per-file stub (a_cs_list, b_cs_list), so a query returns one node and the files sharing the type connect through it (#4247).
  • Internal: added regression coverage locking in cross-module binding of a singly-defined type through re-export chains and the unique-stub rewire; the reported failure (#4262) no longer reproduces on this line.

View release →

v0.9.83 Stable2026-10-09T19:08:05Z

A C# resolution and determinism batch, plus Windows test-suite fixes.

  • Fix: C# a generic and a non-generic type of the same name (Effect vs Effect<T>) now get distinct node ids (arity folded into the id), so they no longer collapse into one node and Effect<T> : Effect no longer produces an inherits self-loop (#4255, #4249, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: C# a call through a member chain (a.b.C()), element access (xs[i].M()), or inside a constructor body now resolves to the right method, fail-closed to a single declared type per hop (collection element types only for T[]/List<T>), instead of being dropped (#4258, #4246, thanks @Mpasha17).
  • Fix: C# a bare call whose name matches an enum member (Delegate(t) next to a Delegate case) no longer binds to the enum member; case members are excluded from both the per-file and cross-file call-resolution maps, fail-closed (#4254, #4245, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: C# a static factory that constructs its own type keeps its method membership edge — an undirected collapse previously let the reverse calls edge overwrite it, hiding the member from every type walk (#4256, #4248, thanks @Mpasha17).
  • Fix: an unqualified call in Java/C#/Scala/C++ binds to the method on the caller's own class chain (own class, then in-file bases, then enclosing classes) instead of the last same-named method declared anywhere in the file; fail-closed on a tie, with free functions and constructors still resolving (#4252, thanks @Yyunozor).
  • Fix: an unresolved re-export target id is now portable — it is minted in a dedicated namespace with a hash over the repo-relative path instead of the absolute checkout path, so a clone produces the same graph (#4257, thanks @andan0).
  • Fix: graphify's own skill runbook now reuses the persisted scan options (excludes and the gitignore flag) a prior build wrote, so a skill-driven update no longer drops opted-in files or re-adds explicitly excluded ones versus a CLI rebuild (#4250, #4240, thanks @deepanshupal).
  • Fix: the test suite passes on Windows — _atomic_replace refuses a read-only destination there instead of silently clobbering it (nt-only guard, no POSIX change), plus encoding, path-shape, and non-regular-file test guards (#4260, thanks @SoloDrex52).
  • Fix: C# nested types imported with using static now resolve (using static Demo.Layer; reaching Layer.Inner), fail-closed on ambiguity, complementing the enclosing-namespace resolution also in this release (#4235, #4216, thanks @hopstreax).
  • Fix: the AST cache directory is now namespaced by the installed tree-sitter grammar versions (...-g<fingerprint>), so upgrading a grammar within the same graphify release no longer serves stale or ABI-incompatible cached ASTs for unchanged files (#4239, #4236, thanks @nothariharan).

obra/superpowers ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v7.0.0 Stable2026-10-10T00:28:58Z

We rebuilt brainstorming from scratch so it does a much better job of what it was always for: helping you work out what you actually want and put it into words before anything gets built. The new skill asks you to describe what you're after and why, plays back what it heard so you can correct it, and keeps asking good questions until the picture is clear. Then it matches the process to the work, from just doing it to writing a full design.

This release also adds a native plugin manifest for the Antigravity Marketplace and fixes Windows hook discovery, Git Bash paths, Hermes skill descriptions, and several smaller bugs.

Brainstorming

  • Brainstorming draws out what you want before it proposes anything. Its first message offers to skip the questions and asks one open question about a real moment or a concrete picture. It offers a menu only when you're stuck. Along the way, it offers to look at prior art, your project, or the web. As it understands each part, it plays that part back in a few hundred words and marks its guesses as guesses. (#2463)
  • It sizes the work after it understands what you want, and says so in plain words. It does a quick, clear task right away, agrees a small change with you in chat, and writes a design document for a project. You can override its call, and it steps up a size if the work grows. (#2463)
  • A builder check replaces the spec-document reviewer. A fresh subagent reads the design as the person who'll build it and lists what they'd still need to ask. Brainstorming answers what it can, makes the minor calls itself and marks them as its own, and brings you the questions that change what gets built, in one round. (#2463)
  • It finds out which choices about how the thing gets made you want to own. Platform, language, libraries, medium: if you have strong views, it talks them through; if you hand them over, it picks sensible defaults and tells you what it picked. It does this even when you skip the questions. We made this change after a session designed an iOS app, never asked about platform, and built a web app. (#2482, #2483)
  • It offers the visual companion whenever seeing would help more than reading: screens, layouts, flows, options that look different, diagrams. The offer drops its token-cost warning. (#2463)
  • The visual companion now shows screens containing $', $&, and similar sequences intact. The server inserted content with String.replace, which treats those sequences as replacement patterns. It now inserts content literally. Thanks @andrew-yian for the report and @luochen211 for the fix. (#2362, #2364)

Antigravity

  • agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers now installs Superpowers as a native Antigravity plugin. We added .antigravity-plugin/plugin.json with the Marketplace display name, logo, and suggested prompts. Previously, agy fell back to importing the repo as a Gemini CLI extension, then rejected the copied Claude-format hooks file on every session with invalid hook "hooks": command hook must specify 'command'. The install command stays the same. (#2479)
  • Superpowers bootstraps on Antigravity through skill discovery. Antigravity has no session-start hook event, but it shows the model each installed skill's description, and using-superpowers' "Use when starting any conversation" prompts the model to load it. We verified this on agy 1.3.1 across 12 runs: "Let's make a react todo list" and "add a settings page" triggered brainstorming before any code, and a failing test triggered systematic-debugging before any edit. We also corrected the README and porting guide, which described a session-start hook and install script that never existed. (#2479)

Hooks

  • SessionStart now works when the harness launches it with a broken PATH. The hooks no longer look up dirname, cat, or bash on PATH, so a startup PATH that can't resolve them (anthropics/claude-code#43127) no longer drops the bootstrap. Thanks @kannan983 for the report and Ada Sen for the fix. (#2310, #2349)
  • Windows: run-hook.cmd finds per-user Git for Windows installs and skips WSL launchers. It now checks %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Git, and when it searches PATH, it skips the WSL bash.exe launchers, which fail without a Linux distro. Thanks @jp5247 for the report, and @citizen204 (#1864) and @KaiyiQuan (#2365) for the fixes we combined here. (#1863, #2393)
  • Windows: run-hook.cmd ignores bash and where in the current directory. Previously, a repository could plant bash.cmd or where.bat and have it run at session start. (#2393)
  • Windows: run-hook.cmd now passes hook exit codes to the harness. It used to report success even when the hook failed. (#2393)

Subagent-Driven Development

  • sdd-workspace leaves a repo's own .superpowers/sdd/.gitignore alone. It used to overwrite the file with * on every run, reverting any version a repo committed (for example, to track progress.md ledgers). It now writes the default only when no file exists. Thanks @aruizcu1989 for the fix. (#2161, #2399)
  • Plan markers stay repo-relative on Windows. On Git Bash, sdd-workspace compared git rev-parse's C:/… root with the plan's /c/… path, so every workspace marker recorded an absolute, machine-specific path. It now resolves the root the same way as the plan path. We found this while landing @t0domanh's Windows test fixes (#2149).

Executing Plans

  • task-done now records tasks whose test command passes silently. When a passing command printed nothing, task-done exited 1 without writing the ledger line, so a finished task looked unfinished. It now records → (no output). Thanks @KenM-BT for the report and Ada Sen for the fix. (#2385, #2388)

Requesting Code Review

  • The example's base-SHA command survives skill arguments. Claude Code replaces $1 in a skill body with the second argument word, so invoking the skill with arguments turned awk '{print $1}' into awk '{print <word>}'. The example now uses cut -d' ' -f1, which contains no $. Thanks @errmakov for the report and @klemens-floege for the fix. (#2311, #2361)

Systematic Debugging

  • The multi-layer diagnostic example no longer prints the secret it checks for. ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET} and env | grep IDENTITY both echoed the signing identity's value into logs. The example now reports only whether the variable is set. Thanks @kennyg-g for the report and @m2dumpling for the fix. (#2375, #2380)

Hermes Agent

  • Hermes' skill list now shows Superpowers skill descriptions. Hermes lists each plugin skill with the description passed to register_skill, which defaults to empty. The plugin passed only a name and path, so every skill appeared blank and the model had nothing to choose from. The plugin now passes each skill's frontmatter description. Thanks @pepijn-blom for the fix. (#2284)

6.3.0 (2026-10-09)

⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

  • captures: Historical captures without current producer accounting or transaction identity, and web diffs missing accessibility or storage dimensions, are rejected. Preserve original captures and recapture with the current producer; update comparison consumers to include every dimension rather than synthesizing missing observations. See the process capture guide and browser scenario contract. (3283a45)
  • browser: JSON shape paths now contain typed property and array-element segments. WebMCP input_schema_shape is replaced by input_schema and input_schema_sha256, retaining declared examples and defaults.
  • process: Filesystem digest omission entries now require system_code; budget and changed-file omissions use null, and unavailable-file omissions preserve the operating-system error code.
  • contracts: Provider analysis outputs must explicitly supply metadata previously repaired with defaults; unsupported nullable facets must be reported as null.
  • javascript: Semantic graph facts now store evidence context IDs and locations. Graph and semantic trace results require an inline evidence_contexts table.
  • contracts: source-map URLs now live in target observations selected by declared_url_sha256, and doctor skill identity no longer emits installed_catalog_digest. Use the documented observation join and identity.skill.state instead.
  • javascript: remove the never-incremented truncated_scopes statistic from JavaScript application analysis results and schemas.
  • native: Objective-C attribute tokens now contain only name and value. Properties report nullable atomicity and readonly facts; class flags, ivar counts, and method requirement flags are nullable when unobserved.

rea-agents-6.2.0rea-agents: v6.2.0 Stable2026-10-09T16:51:14Z

6.2.0 (2026-10-09)

⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

Read the 6.1 to 6.2 migration guide before upgrading. REA's always-bump-minor policy includes breaking changes; 6.2 is not a backward-compatibility promise. Preserve original saved files and regenerate missing observations rather than fabricating identities or facts.

  • MCP / Evidence / snapshots / artifacts: Success results are direct canonical Evidence; read normalized_result rather than the old result/evidence wrapper. Evidence requires nullable analysis_profile, session provider aliases are removed, snapshots require complete profile-bound query records, and artifact roles/permissions belong to occurrences. Recreate incompatible saved data; adding fields without recomputing their semantic identity is invalid. (63bf914)
  • Process captures: Legacy v3 conversion is removed. Explicit executable identity and event_journal are required; retain old captures and recapture when current comparisons are needed instead of inventing launch identity or event order. (2a77469)
  • Cleanup and evaluation: A one-shot analysis reports cleanup failure while preserving the completed observation or primary diagnostic. Handle cleanup_incomplete and retained observations/resources. Configured agent-evaluation fixtures require Evidence-backed correctness, not routing or answer wording alone. (#1211, 27a9cea)
  • JavaScript: Return-field projections require explicit presence; export-shape changes carry both sides' presence and property inventory coverage. Semantic object operations retain complete property_path segments. Regenerate old analysis and distinguish unknown values from unknown presence. (475a0f8)
  • Function comparisons: Remove the unreachable truncated dimension state and summary.truncated counter; update enum and display consumers while retaining explicit unknown facts. (5510b27)
  • Historical sources: Unreadable/unknown symlink targets require target: null; external targets retain the observed absolute target. Reimport graphs containing display placeholders such as <outside-root> and handle nullable targets. (b7b4333)

astral-sh/uv ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
0.13.0 Stable2026-10-09T19:49:55Z

Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-09.

uv 0.13.0 makes Python 3.15 the default stable Python version. We've also included several breaking changes to improve correctness, performance, and compatibility, described below.

We expect most users to be able to upgrade without making changes.

While not a breaking change, this release also updates the format of many of uv's cache entries to improve performance. uv may download or rebuild dependencies after upgrading, because some cached entries from earlier versions cannot be reused. Multiple versions of uv can still safely share the same cache directory.

There are no breaking changes to the configuration of the uv build backend. If your [build-system] table includes an upper bound on uv_build, update it to allow uv_build 0.13, e.g., uv_build>=0.13.0,<0.14.

Breaking changes

  • Use Python 3.15 as the default stable version

    The default stable Python version has changed from 3.14 to 3.15. This affects Python downloads when no version is requested or pinned, e.g., when running uv python install.

    uv continues to use compatible Python installations that are already present. For example, uv venv can still use an installed Python 3.14. If no suitable interpreter is installed and automatic downloads are enabled, commands such as uv venv and uvx python can now download Python 3.15.

    You can opt out of this behavior by requesting Python 3.14 explicitly, e.g., uv venv --python 3.14. For projects, use uv python pin 3.14 to record the version in .python-version.

  • Honor --require-hashes in included constraints files (#22275)

    Previously, uv ignored --require-hashes in constraints files included with -c from a requirements file. Now, uv honors the directive and requires hashes for all requirements in the installation. Installs that previously succeeded can now fail if a requirement is missing a hash.

    You cannot opt out while the directive is present. Add the missing hashes to your requirements, or remove the --require-hashes directive from the included constraints file if hash checking is not intended.

  • Prefer native Python on Windows ARM64 (#22100)

    Previously, ARM64 builds of uv preferred emulated x86_64 Python installations because native wheel support was limited. Now, uv prefers native ARM64 (aarch64) interpreters across Python versions.

    This follows similar changes in CPython, the official Windows Python install manager, and GitHub's actions/setup-python.

    When a native interpreter is unavailable, uv continues to fall back to x86_64, then 32-bit x86.

    You can opt out of this behavior by setting UV_PYTHON_ARCH=x86_64 or requesting an explicit architecture, e.g., cpython-3.14-windows-x86_64. If you are using setup-uv, you can set python-arch: x86_64 instead.

  • Reject editable requirements in included constraints files (#22282)

    Previously, uv silently ignored editable (-e) requirements in constraints files included with -c from a requirements file. Now, uv rejects these requirements with an error, matching pip's behavior.

    You cannot opt out of this behavior. Move editable requirements to a requirements file passed with -r, or pass them directly with --editable, instead of including them in a constraints file.

  • Omit the distutils startup patch on Python 3.10 and later (#22096)

    Previously, uv installed _virtualenv.py and _virtualenv.pth into every new virtual environment to prevent distutils configuration from changing installation paths. Now, like virtualenv 21.6.0, uv omits these files on Python 3.10 and later, which already ignore the affected configuration keys. This reduces Python startup overhead. Python 3.9 and earlier retain the patch.

    You cannot opt out of this behavior. Existing virtual environments are not modified automatically. Recreate an environment with Python 3.10 or later to remove the patch.

    This stabilizes the no-distutils-patch preview feature.

  • Treat requirement-file option values as single paths (#22290)

    Previously, uv split values passed to --constraint, --override, --exclude, and --build-constraint on spaces, even when quoted. Now, each value is treated as a single path, allowing file paths containing spaces.

    You cannot opt out of this behavior. Repeat the option to provide multiple files. For example, replace -c "a.txt b.txt" with -c a.txt -c b.txt.

    Space-separated lists in UV_CONSTRAINT, UV_OVERRIDE, UV_EXCLUDE, and UV_BUILD_CONSTRAINT remain supported.

  • Use tar-codec for tar archives by default (#22094)

    Previously, uv used astral-tokio-tar to extract tar archives, build source distributions with uv_build, and read their metadata for uv publish. Now, uv uses tar-codec, which applies stricter validation when reading archives.

    uv may now reject archives containing hard links or unsupported tar extensions that previous versions accepted. Source distributions created by uv_build can also have different archive bytes and hashes.

    You can opt out of this behavior by setting UV_LEGACY_TAR_BACKEND=1.

    This stabilizes the tar-codec preview feature.

  • Reject uv build --clear output directories that contain a build source (#22276)

    Previously, uv build --clear could delete a project or input source distribution when the output directory contained the source. Now, uv rejects these output directories, including equivalent paths reached through symlinks, before clearing any build output.

    Select an output directory that does not contain any build sources, or omit --clear.

Python

  • Add CPython 3.15.0 (#22400)

Preview features

  • Require hashes for build dependencies, including transitive dependencies, with --require-build-hashes (#21411)

Performance

  • Speed up revalidation of cached HTTP responses by avoiding rewrites of unchanged payloads (#22130)
  • Reduce allocations when reading cached HTTP responses (#22136)
  • Reduce cache storage for HTTP policies and package records (#22135, #22133)
  • Reduce allocations for cached source distribution revisions (#22131)

Bug fixes

  • Avoid overlong wheel cache lock filenames on Windows (#22134)

Install uv 0.13.0

Install prebuilt binaries via shell script

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.13.0/uv-installer.sh | sh

Install prebuilt binaries via powershell script

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.13.0/uv-installer.ps1 | iex"

Download uv 0.13.0

The artifacts in this release have attestations generated with GitHub Artifact Attestations. These can be verified by using the GitHub CLI:

You can also download the attestation from GitHub and verify against that directly:

code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v5.1.29 Stable2026-10-09T17:49:08Z

Child tasks and Kibitzer wakes of a fast-mode session no longer fail with model_unavailable: a -fast pin is accepted when the session starts on its paired base model. Since 5.1.25, a category pinned to a -fast catalog variant such as chatgpt-subscription/gpt-6-luna-fast was refused after start, because senpi starts a -fast pin on its base model with the priority tier. Kibitzer recall wakes failed on every wake, and the built-in fast-first chains (quick, deep-low, deep-high, ultrabrain) silently skipped their first model. A run that started on the standard tier instead of priority is now accepted and recorded on the task (effective_model.service_tier) instead of refused. (#9793, #9808, #9812, #9813)

omo runs on senpi 2026.10.10-11. tool_schema("eval:environments") now documents packages.install and its environment_install_timeout, so JavaScript and Python cells can discover how to install packages without changing the default eval description or parameters. Julia, Ruby and Python cells do less fixed work per cell: no globals walk below the memory thresholds, no awaited cwd stat, and leaner Python queue and capture bookkeeping. A scheduled prompt created in a desktop thread before the OmO desktop moved that folder now fires, and --session, --resume and --continue find such sessions in the folder's new home. A session another live process already holds is refused with a typed session_held error instead of being opened twice. Sessions that share MCP servers but resolve different MCP configs no longer break each other's tools. A goal whose continuation stops also stops its timer. On Windows, stopping a command's process tree can no longer kill an unrelated process that reused a pid. On macOS and Linux, processes a JavaScript eval cell starts get their own process group, so a group kill can't stop the agent, and leftover grandchildren are stopped when the cell ends. Full engine notes: senpi 2026.10.10-11. (code-yeongyu/senpi#3003, code-yeongyu/senpi#3028, code-yeongyu/senpi#3033, code-yeongyu/senpi#3034, code-yeongyu/senpi#2990, code-yeongyu/senpi#2951, code-yeongyu/senpi#2597, code-yeongyu/senpi#3007, code-yeongyu/senpi#2999, code-yeongyu/senpi#2995, code-yeongyu/senpi#3020, #9825)

Fixed

A background child no longer stays suspended while its parent is running. A child parked while its parent session was still live was only revisited at the parent's next start, so it could sit suspended for hours and a goal waiting on its result waited forever. It is now revived right away, or ends with one result. (#9350, #9799)

omo.dev shows its live stats more reliably. A cold page load whose first stats refresh hit one upstream blip showed the fallback numbers; it now falls back to the last complete set instead. (#9820, #9821)

kenn-io/agentsview ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v0.45.0 Stable2026-10-09T16:21:23Z

New features

  • Choose Español in Settings. Browsers set to Spanish use it on first load.
  • Browse Junie CLI, OMO, and StepCode sessions with their usage and costs. Junie ingestion excludes tool calls and IDE-only conversations. If you previously used PI_DIR for OMO, remove that override to avoid indexing new sessions twice.
  • Read Antigravity conversations from plaintext transcripts when no session database exists, without a decryption key. These transcripts include reasoning and tool calls but no token usage or cost.
  • See commits, lines added and removed, and files changed on the dashboard for the selected dates. Load pull-request totals on demand after GitHub setup.
  • Switch the Activity timeline between concurrency, user-message frequency, and assistant-message frequency.
  • Compare user, assistant, and other message counts in the Analytics timeline with Absolute and Percent views. Other includes system entries and tool results.
  • See all prompt tokens in the Usage page's Total Input card, including cache reads and writes. The previous Input Tokens count is labeled Uncached Input.
  • Choose Smooth, Lines, or Bars for Cost Over Time. The chart remembers your choice, shows zero-spend days, and supports dragging to select a date range.
  • Follow tool errors, retries, switches, and recovery in a session's tool sequences panel. Each step links to its transcript call and shows available timing and evidence. Opening the panel adds no token charges.
  • Give Claude Code and Codex access to past conversations through native conversation-memory plugins. Session-start refresh and readiness diagnostics help identify missing setup or search coverage.
  • Install proactive conversation recall with agentsview skills install. The package guides agents to search relevant history, distinguish proposals from accepted decisions, and cite transcript evidence.
  • Approve or archive extracted entries in Recall, the collection of memories extracted from sessions. Review decisions survive later extraction changes.
  • Activate the first Recall collection before the initial backlog finishes, once a session is complete and usable entries exist. Recent sessions extract first, and later passes add to the active collection.
  • Extract Recall entries from several sessions at once by setting concurrency on an extraction server. The default remains 1.
  • Choose the default CLI for generated insights with [insights] default_agent. Leaving it unset keeps Claude as the default.
  • Replace selected ChatGPT or Claude.ai imports with agentsview import --replace <session-id>. The old transcript moves to Trash as a restorable copy, while the live session keeps its name and pins on matching messages.
  • Identify refused ChatGPT and Claude.ai imports by session ID and reason. CLI summaries separate changed history, shorter exports, trashed sessions, and temporary failures.
  • Use semantic and hybrid search on ClickHouse mirrors. Embeddings upload with clickhouse push when vector search is enabled; --no-vectors or push_vectors = false opts out.
  • Browse hosted raw-sync uploads after the server parses them into PostgreSQL sessions. This opt-in mode removes the need for a local SQLite archive or a separate pg push.
  • Upload existing sources in a finite, resumable run with raw-sync backfill --run-id ID --provider NAME. Start raw-sync watch after the run completes to upload later changes.
  • Inspect hosted uploads and parsing with raw-sync server-status and the raw-sync health API. Run raw-sync clean-uploads to expire upload sessions and remove orphaned temporary files without starting the server.
  • Serve AgentsView under a reverse-proxy subpath with serve --base-path. Keep --public-url origin-only.
  • Search several literal terms within one user/assistant exchange over MCP on SQLite and PostgreSQL. Narrow results by session, branch, project, agent, or date.
  • Read MCP search evidence from the same transcript revision, and continue reading messages beyond the previous 20,000-character limit. Revision checks report when the source changed.
  • Build clients for multiple machines with host keys and session titles in search results, batch session lookup, and optional source size and archive-update metadata.

Improvements

  • Load Activity, Usage, and Analytics reports faster on ClickHouse with lower memory use. Opened past-day reports survive restarts, and new pushes refresh only changed sessions where possible. Upgraded deployments need a push to complete new report data and access to system.parts for serving.
  • Load Tool Usage and Top Skills analytics faster on PostgreSQL, with less memory use on large archives.
  • Load dashboard metadata with less database work on large SQLite archives. The first writable startup builds an index before serving, so that startup takes longer.
  • Open Usage after a price update without waiting for a full cache rebuild. Only sessions using changed models rebuild, and rebuilding starts in the background. The first startup after upgrading rebuilds the usage cache once.
  • Sync and rebuild large archives with less retained transcript data and less repeated processing. Fresh archives defer the conversation export index until the first export, and full resync removes the redundant stored copy of message text.
  • Update Cursor IDE chats with less parsing and memory use. A database change reparses only chats whose saved documents changed.
  • Keep file watching responsive on large Antigravity installs by skipping generated directory trees. Windows watchers also use smaller change buffers, reducing memory use.
  • Build hourly export day and export digest reports faster, especially for long sessions.
  • See the current sync stage, subagent-repair counts, and notices when a sync waits for another operation. Refresh controls show elapsed query time and a live request timeline.
  • Load more Activity sessions as you scroll. New pages append to the table, and failed loads offer a retry.
  • See agent-provided session titles consistently, with user-chosen names taking precedence. First-message previews retain the user's actual prompt.
  • Read fuller Codebuff and Freebuff transcripts, including attachment markers, errors, and answers to agent questions. Nested agents appear as linked subagent sessions, and costs include every prompt's reported credits.
  • See OpenCode tool durations from dispatch to result, including permission waits. Calls without a dispatch timestamp retain an unknown duration.
  • Extract fewer Recall procedure entries from work an agent only proposed. Procedure extraction requires tool evidence in the relevant action window. Upgrading re-extracts existing sessions.
  • Keep Recall vector and hybrid queries available while extraction adds entries. The index may trail by 256 changes by default; hybrid search still finds newer entries by keyword.
  • Configure embedding endpoints with HTTPS for public IP addresses and without query strings. Builds leave documents pending when configuration, credentials, or server failures prevent embedding.
  • Sync remote hosts over HTTP. SSH sync is removed; configure each remote with a daemon URL and token. Existing archived sessions remain available.
  • Measure app opens, screen visits, core actions, and visible visit duration through the existing telemetry opt-out. Daily daemon activity counts at most once per installation per UTC day.
  • Diagnose desktop startup and database delays with logs that show backend port selection, readiness results, stalled database checkpoints, and connection or write-lock waits.

Bug fixes

  • Build from a fresh Go module cache without a missing-dependency error.
  • Re-import ChatGPT exports to append new messages, fill previously empty tool results, and restore truncated message text while preserving existing message IDs and pins.
  • Keep saved Claude.ai turns when a stale export contains fewer messages. Shorter exports are refused unless you explicitly request replacement.
  • View, search, and copy raw Codex and Grok tool inputs. Codex patch edits also appear in Recent Edits.
  • Keep both transcripts when Gemini CLI or Cursor files share a session ID, instead of letting one overwrite the other.
  • Read Claude subagent continuations saved under another parent session. Pi subagents in nested directories also appear and link to their parent when the recorded layout identifies it.
  • Keep Claude messages from other sessions out of human prompt counts and session-title selection. The transcript labels them "Message from another session".
  • Count workers launched by another agent as Subagents on Activity, rather than inflating the Interactive peak.
  • Price Codex cache writes at the cache-write rate and estimate auto-review costs using GPT-5.6 Luna rates. Offline reports and exports also include pricing for GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6.1 Sol.
  • Retain reported costs when model filters contain spaces between model names or are blank on SQLite and PostgreSQL.
  • Count every message in term trends for time zones where daylight saving time skips local midnight.
  • Remove permanently deleted sessions from semantic search on the next embedding build. Sessions removed by sync and later imported again receive embeddings again.
  • Keep Cursor and Antigravity idle instead of repeatedly syncing unchanged SQLite databases.
  • Show Cursor IDE sessions on the date of their earliest timestamped message.
  • Update active Codex Desktop sessions on macOS within about 30 seconds, even without Codex history hints.
  • Start background serving on macOS without hanging on permission prompts for external volumes. Enable scan_protected_paths = true to include Git details from those locations.
  • Keep macOS file identities stable across reboots, avoiding repeated archive reparses. Upgrading performs one initial reparse and raw-source capture.
  • Apply session-provider changes made in Settings without restarting the daemon. Separate push-watch processes still require a restart.
  • Keep local sessions and reachable remotes syncing when another remote's hostname cannot resolve. Sync failures retain their actionable error details.
  • Keep Linux servers discoverable after clock corrections, and let Windows startup progress update while commands read it.
  • Detect same-size file replacements on Windows and sync Positron project changes when file timestamps stay the same.
  • Open the desktop app against an authenticated local daemon without a readiness timeout. The app also recovers after an observed backend outage while hidden and avoids stale startup errors during an in-app update.
  • Replace a served DuckDB mirror with duckdb push on Windows without stopping duckdb serve.
  • Load current SQLite-backed OpenClaw sessions and discover Hermes Agent sessions in the default Windows location.
  • Report incomplete Git and pull-request totals in agentsview stats, and wait beyond the former 30-second client timeout for slow results.
  • Count repositories once across clones and worktrees, and count each commit once while retaining work from diverged branches.
  • Clear the minimum-prompt filter by clicking its selected value again. Usage cards grow to contain wrapped text, and password-manager menus no longer cover typeahead search boxes.
  • Refuse writable archives when the build cannot load their existing FTS5 index, with an error that explains how to fix the executable.
